items.question: Even though the crew of the BBC Africa did eventually get the rudder working again, why could they not keep the ship from hitting the Common Faith?
items.expected_answer: The chief officer's repeated attempts to retake control with the in-command FU button failed, and the master only switched to emergency override mode after about a minute; by the time he regained rudder control it was too late to turn the vessel enough to avoid the moored bulk carrier.

evidence.quote: The chief officer attempted to regain control by re- pressing the in-command FU button, without success. After about a minute, the master activated the steering control system’s emergency override mode. Although he was able to regain control of the rudder, it was too late to sufficiently turn the vessel before colliding with the moored bulk carrier Common Faith.

items.notes: Tests a causal passage spanning a chunk boundary in the analysis (delay in using emergency override).

items.question: Where was the BBC Africa fixed up after its collision in Houston, and when was that work finished?
items.expected_answer: Its repairs were done at a shipyard in Swinemunde, Poland, and were completed in November 2023.

evidence.quote: Repairs performed in the shipyard in Swinemunde, Poland, were completed in November 2023.

items.notes: Tests retrieval of a single repair-location detail from the damage section.
